title: Advance Payments & Retainers: Controls, Procurement Flow, and Revenue Recognition Guidance
author: Amina Patel
body:
Overview:

This guidance establishes Redwood Inference’s required controls, procurement flow, contract language, and accounting treatment for advance payments (including retainers and prepaid service arrangements). Purpose is to reduce revenue recognition risk, improve cash-to-revenue transparency, and standardize procurement and legal review for prepayment scenarios.

Scope:

- Applies to all negotiating parties that obligate Redwood to accept or disburse advance payments, retainers, deposits, or prepaid service fees across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private offerings.
- Includes customer-facing contracts, reseller/partner agreements, and vendor prepayment arrangements.

Key definitions:

- Advance payment: Any cash or cash-equivalent received prior to full delivery of contracted goods or services.
- Retainer: An upfront payment to secure availability of services for a defined period.
- Deferred revenue: Liability recorded when cash is received before satisfaction of performance obligations.
- Prepaid expense: Payment made in advance for goods or services Redwood will consume (vendor prepayment).

High-level policy statements:

1) All customer advance payments must be captured and tracked in the Deferred Revenue subledger within 3 business days of receipt.
2) Contract terms that include advance payments or retainers must be reviewed by Legal for clause alignment and by Finance for accounting impact prior to signature.
3) Procurement of vendor prepayments > USD 25,000 requires VP Finance approval and Security sign-off when the vendor will handle customer data.
4) Refund, netting, and escrow language standards must be used for advances > USD 100,000.

Approval matrix (summary):

- Up to USD 25,000: Product Manager + Procurement Lead signoff.
- USD 25,001 to USD 100,000: Head of Procurement + Finance Manager + Legal review.
- > USD 100,000: VP Finance + GC (General Counsel) + CRO (if customer impact).

(See sample approval table below for required artifacts.)

Procurement & Contract intake flow (required steps):

1. Business submits PR/Deal Intake with: SOW, proposed payment schedule, legal redlines, vendor security questionnaire (if vendor), and forecasted revenue recognition impact (Finance template).
2. Procurement validates vendor onboarding, tax/VAT questions, and completes supplier risk assessment.
3. Legal performs advance-payment clause review and inserts standard language (section below).
4. Finance performs recognition assessment (ASC 606 analysis), determines GL coding and deferred revenue schedule, and uploads prelim journal entries to NetSuite.
5. Approvals per matrix obtained.
6. PO/Customer Order and Payment Instructions issued. Cash recorded by Treasury; accounting entry created within 3 business days.

Required artifacts for approval (checklist):

- Fully executed contract or redline summary.
- Statement of Work or scope with acceptance criteria.
- Payment schedule and bank instructions.
- Finance revenue allocation worksheet (template in attachments).
- Vendor security questionnaire and remediation plan (if applicable).

Standard contract language (recommended clauses):

1) Advance Payment / Retainer Clause (example):

  "Customer shall pay an initial retainer equal to X% of the estimated fees upon execution. Such retainer will be held as a prepayment and applied to invoices as Services are performed. Refunds of unused retainer amounts will be made within 30 days of contract termination unless otherwise stated."

2) Escrow / Custodial Holders (for > USD 100,000):

  "If an advance exceeds USD 100,000, the parties shall place funds in a mutually agreeable escrow account or provide a bank guarantee. Escrow release terms will be tied to milestone acceptance."

3) Netting / Setoff Rights:

  "Redwood reserves the right to set off amounts owed to Customer against any outstanding unpaid obligations, subject to notice and applicable law."

4) Data & Security Addendum (if vendor holds customer data):

  "Vendor shall: comply with Redwood’s Data Processing Addendum, encrypt customer data at rest and in transit, and provide SOC2 Type II evidence within 30 days of request."

Accounting treatment (principles):

- Follow ASC 606 / IFRS 15 principles: identify the contract, separate performance obligations, determine the transaction price, allocate to performance obligations, and recognize when/ as obligations are satisfied.
- Typical treatments:
  - Annual support prepayment: Recognize ratably over support term (monthly amortization).
  - Retainer for on-call engineering: Recognize as services are delivered (transfer of control) — use usage-backed recognition if measurable.
  - Prepaid implementation milestone schedule: Recognize at the point of milestone acceptance if distinct.

Sample journal entries (simplified):

1) Receipt of advance payment from customer (cash receipt):

  Dr Cash (Bank)             USD 120,000
  Cr Deferred Revenue        USD 120,000

2) Recognize monthly revenue for annual support (12 months):

  Dr Deferred Revenue        USD 10,000
  Cr Revenue — Support       USD 10,000

3) Refund of unused portion of retainer (if customer terminates early):

  Dr Deferred Revenue        USD 6,000
  Cr Cash (Bank)             USD 6,000

4) Vendor prepayment for a specialized integration (expensed over useful life):

  Dr Prepaid Expense — Vendor USD 50,000
  Cr Cash (Bank)             USD 50,000

  Amortize monthly to Expense:
  Dr Integration Expense     USD 5,000
  Cr Prepaid Expense         USD 5,000

GL codes (recommended mapping examples):

- 2100 – Deferred Revenue — Customer Prepayments
- 2101 – Deferred Revenue — Retainers
- 1300 – Prepaid Expenses — Vendor Prepayments
- 4000 – Revenue — Support & Maintenance
- 4010 – Revenue — Professional Services

Revenue recognition templates & artifacts:

- Use the Finance "RevRec Assessment" spreadsheet for any deal including advance payments. The template captures performance obligations, allocation, and a recognition schedule. Link: /finance/revrec/templates/revrec-assessment-2025.xlsx
- Attach completed template to deal folder in NetSuite/DealRoom before routing for signature.

Billing & Invoicing requirements (customer-facing):

Required invoice fields when billing prepayments or applying retainer credits:

- Customer name and billing address
- Contract/PO number and SOW reference
- Invoice date and due date
- Line-level description showing: base fee, retainer applied, remaining retainer balance
- Amounts allocated to deferred revenue and amounts recognized as revenue this period
- GL mapping line (internal use)

Sample invoice narrative:

  "Invoice for Professional Services — Retainer application: Initial retainer USD 120,000 applied as credit for January 2026 services; remaining retainer balance USD 110,000."

Controls, monitoring, and KPIs:

- Monthly subledger reconciliation: Revenue Ops performs a deferred revenue subledger reconciliation by the 10th business day of each month.
- Aging report: Any deferred balance older than 90 days without a matching performance obligation or milestone triggers an investigation.
- Exception SLA: Investigation started within 3 business days; remediation completed within 15 business days, or escalate to VP Finance.
- Quarterly internal audit: select 10% of advance payment deals for audit each quarter (min 8 deals).

Escalation & exceptions procedure:

1) Discovery: Finance flags item via monthly reconciliation and adds to the "RevRec Exceptions" tracker.
2) Initial owner outreach: Revenue Ops pings deal owner (Sales or Customer Success) to provide SOW or evidence of performance.
3) If no resolution in 10 business days, Finance + Legal triage and propose remediation: either recognize on acceptance, refund, or contract amendment.
4) >30 days unresolved: Escalate to VP Finance and Legal for decision on reserve or write-off.

Operational examples & edge cases:

- Multi-year prepayment with annual renewals: allocate contract price across each year based on standalone selling price methodology and update allocation on material contract changes.
- Customer-credit note application: apply credit to deferred revenue balance first, then to outstanding AR. Document application in ticketing system.
- Currency & FX: advances received in foreign currency are recorded at receipt FX rate; translation of deferred amounts for reporting per the accounting policy (see FX policy).

IT/system requirements & recommended configuration:

- NetSuite: enable deferred revenue subledger and recognition schedules tied to contract IDs. All advance payments must reference the contract ID.
- Deal Room / CLM: tag contracts that include prepayments with metadata: payment_type=advance, bucket=deferred, escrow_required=(yes/no).
- Treasury: provide daily cash posting feed to Finance to minimize recording delay.

Responsibilities & owners:

- Revenue Operations (owner): maintain deferred revenue subledger and monthly reconciliations.
- Procurement: vendor onboarding, PO issuance for vendor prepayments.
- Legal: contract clause standardization and redline approval.
- Sales / CS: provide SOWs, acceptance evidence, and operational coordination for performance obligations.
- Treasury: cash receipt posting and banking controls.

Training & rollout:

- All Sales, Revenue Ops, Legal, Procurement, and Finance staff must complete the "RevRec & Advance Payments" training (learning module ID: FIN-ADV-2026) within 60 days of publication.
- Playbooks and quick-reference cards will be published in the Finance team wiki and linked from the deal intake form.

Appendix A — Quick checklist for deal desk (short):

1. Does deal include advance/retainer? Yes/No.
2. Forecasted advance amount and currency.
3. Completed RevRec Assessment attached.
4. Approval per matrix obtained.
5. Payment instructions and escrow (if required) documented.
6. GL codes and recognition schedule confirmed.

Appendix B — Example contract snippet (copy-paste safe):

"Payment and Retainer: Customer will pay an initial retainer equal to 20% of the estimated fees upon execution. Redwood will record receipt as a prepayment and apply amounts to invoices as Services are performed. Refunds of unused prepayments will be made in accordance with the Refund Schedule in Schedule B, unless the parties agree otherwise in writing"

End of document.
